findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1356-1359 (the last two steps of "While this Foundry opens its secrets key, starting over is not offered and changes nothing"), with its acceptance row docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md:424 and the S2 route-table impact docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/architecture.md:2838
findings.obligation: The S2 acceptance row for the healthy-key state: "Both the start over address and a post to it answer this Foundry's integrations page, with the stored key, the Activity and the version every replica follows as they were" - an S2 row whose disposition is Tested, so S2 craft must bring it to GREEN inside the S2 targets.
findings.observation: The scenario's second When posts to /admin/instance/integrations/secrets-key/start-over and its Then requires the integrations page, but the S2 design registers only the GET of that door: the S2 route-table impact reads "The GET of the start-over door is registered behind the same guard; its POST lands with S3", and the S3 impact (architecture.md:3243) reads "The POST of the start-over door joins its GET on the same route". The router composes each door with get(...).post(...) on one route (crates/foundry-app/src/lib.rs:858-862 for the replace door) and sets no method-not-allowed fallback, only .fallback(uniform_not_found) for unmatched paths (lib.rs:978), so after S2 ships the GET alone a POST to that path answers 405 with no body - neither the integrations page nor a page containing "Integrations for this Foundry". then_answers_integrations_page therefore fails, the us-iis-07 lane stays red, and S2 cannot pass its own gate: the crafter must either exceed the slice's recorded targets or report S2 not green. The GET half of this scenario is exactly the remedy the previous round named and it closes the blocking finding on its own; the POST half is the overshoot.
findings.remediation: Keep the GET half and drop the POST half from the S2 row: remove the two steps "When Priya posts a start over request anyway" and the Then pair that follows it from the scenario, and remove "and a post to it" from the acceptance row's expected text, so the kept-link POST on a healthy Foundry is observed where its route exists - S3, which already owns the start-over POST and its refusals. The InstanceDoor::StartOver arm and the remember() it added stay, S3 needs them. Alternative, by agreement with DESIGN rather than by the oracle alone: DESIGN moves the does-not-apply arm of the start-over POST into the S2 route-table impact, and the row then stands unchanged. Either way, record the disposition on the S2 row.
